item.text: {"text":"Recent evidence supports separating recommendation choice from utility: a 231-participant study found persuasive explanations increased selection of lower-utility options, so positive reactions alone do not establish immediate usefulness ([Rahman et al., 2026](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijhcs.2025.103720)). A proposed diagnostic taxonomy—not an established taxonomy from these papers—is: immediate choice, requiring explicit current intent; broad relevance, supported by interests but no immediate commitment; explicit mismatch, requiring a stated conflict; insufficient information, when evidence cannot resolve suitability. Attach evidence from recorded feedback, histories, titles, descriptions, or timestamps to each label. Ownership and compatibility remain unknown without explicit evidence. Abstention needs evaluation: [AbstentionBench, 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09038) found persistent failures across underspecified and unanswerable questions, with prompting insufficient to solve uncertainty recognition.\n\nNo directly matching prospective, budget-matched study of diagnostic guidance versus a gated recent-history baseline emerged from this search. Evaluation guidance calls for equal treatment of algorithms in tuning, runtime, and hardware ([Improving Methodological Standards, 2026](https://doi.org/10.1145/3800587)). A suitable prospective experiment would freeze the taxonomy, intervention menu, and selection rules before new trials; compare diagnostic guidance, the gated baseline, and shuffled-diagnostic guidance under equal total GPU budgets, counting diagnostics and failures. Select using the same four-category macro validation HR@10; reserve hidden tests for final host evaluation. Report paired gains across repeated searches, category outcomes, and uncertainty. Twenty feedback users provide exploratory diagnostic evidence; they cannot establish population-level utility or latent user traits."}
